stem: Which system of equations represents this situation, where $x$ is the number of short recordings and $y$ is the number of long recordings?
stimulus: A folklore studies team recorded 40 storytellers telling local legends. Each short recording lasted 15 minutes, and each long recording lasted 45 minutes. Together, all 40 recordings lasted 16 hours.
explanation: First name the variables: $x$ is the number of short recordings and $y$ is the number of long recordings. The count equation adds up the recordings: $x + y = 40$. The value equation adds up the time. Each short recording gives 15 minutes and each long one gives 45 minutes, so the total time is $15x + 45y$ minutes. The total is given in hours, so you have to convert it before you can set the two sides equal: 16 hours × 60 = 960 minutes. That gives $15x + 45y = 960$. (Check: 28 short and 12 long recordings make 40 recordings, and $420 + 540 = 960$ minutes.)

A.why: Your count equation is correct, but you swapped the rates in the time equation. You put the 45-minute length on the short recordings ($x$) and the 15-minute length on the long ones ($y$). Match each rate to the variable it describes: the short recordings get 15.

B.why: You swapped the two totals. 960 minutes is the total time, not the number of recordings, so it can't be what $x + y$ equals. The count equation has to use the 40 recordings, and the time equation has to use the time total.

D.why: You set up both equations correctly but didn't convert the units. $15x + 45y$ measures minutes, and 16 is in hours. Convert 16 hours to $16 \times 60 = 960$ minutes before you set the two sides equal.

subtype_name: Pick the system that models the story
